newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB says to cut July debenture coupon to 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: LTCB says to cut July debenture coupon to 2.2 pct.

text.p: The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) said on Wednesday that it would cut the coupon rate for its July five-year bank debentures to 2.2 percent from 2.4 percent in June.
The LTCB also said it would cut its long-term prime lending rate for July to 2.7 percent from 2.9 percent previously, effective from Thursday.

On Tuesday, the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, the largest of Japan's three long-term credit banks, said it would cut the coupon rate of its July five-year bank debentures to 1.8 percent from two percent, and its July long-term prime rate to 2.7 percent from 2.9 percent.
The long-term prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
The prime rate, which is also a key reference point for other banks making long-term loans, was last cut by 0.2 percentage point to 2.9 percent in June.
LTCB's June five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of 2.4 percent were bid at 2.25 percent on Wednesday morning, bond traders said.
